The idea in one picture

You create the shop in the portal and send the owner a link. The owner pastes it on the shop computer. From then on the shop copies itself to the cloud, all day, by itself.

Connect a shop: 6 steps

You steps happen in the portal. Owner steps happen on the shop computer, in Coduo POS.

1

Add the client You

Sign in to the portal and press New client. Enter the shop's name, then pick how many months of Online they paid for (1, 3, 6, 12, or none yet). Press Create client and get the connection link.

That also creates their till, Main till, so there is nothing else to set up.

2

Send the link You

The next screen prints the link like a till receipt. Press Copy link, or Send on WhatsApp to send it with instructions in English and Arabic.

Shown once.The link works one time and expires after 7 days. If you lose it, press Create connection link again; the old one stops working.
3

Open Settings → Online Owner

On the shop computer, in Coduo POS, an administrator opens Settings and picks the Online tab. It explains the three steps and has one box for the link. Cashiers do not see this tab.

4

Paste the link and press Connect Owner

Paste what was received. Pasting the whole WhatsApp message is fine: Coduo POS finds the link inside it. Then press Connect.

Pasted the wrong thing?It says so in plain words and keeps what was typed, so a typo can be fixed. Nothing changes until it works.
5

It connects, and the shop uploads Owner

Within seconds the screen shows Connected, the shop name and Everything has been sent. Nothing to restart.

  • Last sent: the last time the cloud confirmed receiving data.
  • Subscription: the plan and its end date.
  • Send now pushes immediately; otherwise it sends by itself every 30 seconds.
6

Check it in the portal You

Open the till's page. You should see Connected, In contact and a recent last contact. What the cloud holds shows the shop's products, customers and orders as counts; they should match the till.

Reading the portal

The portal is built so that most days you open it, see nothing needs you, and close it.

!

"Needs you" comes first You

The top of the Clients page lists only what needs an action, with a button for it. Red is urgent, amber can wait a day. It appears when:

  • a subscription has ended (or is in its grace week), or ends within 14 days;
  • a connected till has had no contact for over a day;
  • a link was sent but not used for 2 days, or expired unused;
  • a client has no till yet.

A client you deactivated or a till you disabled never appears here: that was on purpose.

24

The 24-hour strip You

Every till has a row of 24 boxes, one per hour, ending with the current hour. It shows when the shop's PC could be reached, so a power cut or an internet outage shows up as a grey gap. Hover a box for the hour.

in contactin contact, busy hournot reached: PC off, no power or no internetthis hour

A connected PC checks in about every 10 minutes even when the shop is quiet. So a shop that closes at night and a PC that lost power look different from a shop that simply sold nothing: the first has grey hours, the second does not.

≡

The client list You

One row per client: plan and end date, the strip, and the last contact. Type in the box to search; the chips filter to Connected, Waiting for a link or Needs you. Times are shown in Beirut time (change it with Cloud__TimeZone).

Day to day

Renewing is the one thing you will do regularly.

+

Renewing a client You

Open the client and press +1 mo, +3 mo, +6 mo or +12 mo. A message confirms it ("Added 12 months. Online now ends 2027-11-06").

  • Renewing early keeps the time they had left. Renewing late starts today, so nobody pays for a gap.
  • What the till saved while it was not allowed to send goes through right after.
  • Suspend stops syncing at once. Their till keeps selling.

Buttons that cut something off ask first You

Disconnect, Disable, Suspend, Deactivate and issuing a raw token each ask for confirmation and say exactly what will happen, and that the shop keeps selling.

Other situations

Open the till's page in the portal; every button below is there.

The shop got a new PC

Press Reconnect this till (new link) and send the link. The old PC's access stops when the new one connects.

The owner pastes it on the new PC, as in steps 3 to 5.

A second till

Open the client and use Add a till. Each till gets its own link and its own copy.

Tills are not merged: two tills means two separate copies. Sharing one database between PCs of the same store is planned, see "What comes next".

The till restored an old backup

Press Request full resync. At its next contact the till wipes this shop's cloud copy and uploads everything again.

Without this the cloud keeps data the restored till no longer has.

Stop the service for a shop

Disconnect removes the till's access at once. Suspend (on the client) pauses the subscription. Disable blocks the till.

Their till keeps selling in every case.

The owner wants to leave

On the till: Settings → Online → Disconnect. It asks first and says nothing on the till is deleted.

Also press Disconnect in the portal, and remove their data from the cloud yourself.

The owner's Coduo POS is in Arabic

The Online tab switches language and direction with the rest of the app. The link box stays left-to-right.

The Arabic wording has not been proofread by a native speaker yet.

Upgrades are protected

When Coduo POS updates itself on a client's PC, it changes the structure of their database. This is the moment data could be lost, so it is guarded.

1. A copy first

Before any change, Coduo POS copies the whole database to pre-upgrade-backups (next to it) and checks the copy is complete.

If the copy cannot be made (for example the disk is full), the upgrade does not run and the data is untouched. Coduo POS says why.

2. A check after

After the upgrade it checks the database is sound, no table lost rows, and no record points at something that is gone.

If anything is wrong, the copy is put back automatically.

3. Power cut in the middle

If the power dies during an upgrade, the next start finds the unfinished upgrade and puts the copy back before trying again.

The newest 5 copies are kept.

Not a promise of zero risk.It makes a failed upgrade undoable. It cannot help if the copy folder is deleted or the disk itself fails; that is what ordinary backups are for.

Starting the cloud (once, not per shop)

The portal and the cloud copies live in one small program. Run it somewhere the shops can reach over the internet.

Try it on your own PC

Good for practising these steps. It only works with a till on the same computer.

$env:Cloud__AdminUser = "owner"
$env:Cloud__AdminPassword = "a-long-password"
$env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = "Development"
dotnet run --project Cloud --urls http://localhost:5100

Then open http://localhost:5100 and sign in.

On a real server

Any small Linux server with Docker and a domain name. Put three lines in a .env file (CLOUD_DOMAIN, CLOUD_ADMIN_USER, CLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD), then:

docker compose -f Cloud/docker-compose.yml up -d --build

HTTPS is set up automatically. Shops must use an https:// link. This Docker setup has not been run yet: build it once and open /healthz before relying on it.

Back up first.Everything lives in one folder (the cloud-data volume): the client list and every shop's copy. Back it up before the first paying client.

What comes next Not built yet

Stores with several PCs. This is the agreed design, not something you can use today.

The rule.Each store has one main database, on one PC in the store (the store server). The other PCs (tills) use it over the shop network. Only the store server talks to the cloud. So an internet cut changes nothing for the tills, and nothing ever has to be merged.

In the portal

You mark which PC of a store is the server and register the other PCs as tills with the same kind of link.

Open questions

Printing receipts from a till (the server prints today), how licences count tills, and how the PCs find each other on the shop network.

If the server PC dies

A standby PC that copies it continuously, promoted by you with one button. Not automatic, on purpose.

Full design, including the order of work: docs/online/STORE-SERVER.md.

The whole thing, on one card

  1. You Portal → New client → Create client and get the connection link.
  2. You Send on WhatsApp.
  3. Owner Coduo POS → Settings → Online, paste, Connect.
  4. You Open the till's page: Connected and In contact.
  5. After that, open the portal when you like. Needs you tells you what to do; +12 mo renews.
Good to know:Selling never waits for Online. If the internet drops, sales are kept on the shop PC and sent later. Passwords and PINs never leave the shop. What the owner can see online (the phone app) is not built yet: today the cloud holds the copy.
